newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SKODA PLANS MODEST START TO RUSSIAN OUTPUT(SEE MY291647).
newsitem.headline: SKODA PLANS MODEST START TO RUSSIAN OUTPUT(SEE MY291647).

text.p: Czech car maker Skoda Auto a.s., a unit of Germany's Volkswagen AG, plans to start modest production in Russia next year although sales there could eventually reach tens of thousands, a spokesman said on Friday.

Spokesman Milan Smutny said that Skoda hoped to sell 10,000 of its Felicia and Octavia models in Russia next year, twice this year's sales, but most would be from its existing factory in the Czech town of Mlada Boleslav.

"We hope it will be possible to start assembly production early next year in Russia," he told Reuters. Asked what Russian production would be next year, he said: "We would like to start with hundreds of cars."
Eventually sales could climb to tens of thousands but this was years away and depended on the market, official approvals, training workers, building up a dealer network and so on.
No decisions have yet been made on the site for production, which is planned for existing factories lying idle due to economic reform in Russia, although Smolensk is a frontrunner.
Skoda planned to follow the model of its assembly plant in the Polish city of Poznan, said Smutny. Polish production began modestly but is now rising sharply.

Smutny noted that selling Czech-made cars on the Russian market was difficult as they attracted tariffs of between 80 and 100 percent. Sales are currently of the Felicia hatchback but Smutny said Skoda hoped to launch its mid-size Octavia model in Russia next summer.
